HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 84 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. - 10999 of 2021 Applicant :- Dr Rajendra Kumar Gupta @ Dr Rajan Gupta And 2 Others Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Another Counsel for Applicant :- Pratik Chandra,Asha Parihar Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Pawankumar Dubey Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

This application has been moved on behalf of the applicant 1. Dr. Rajendra Kumar Gupta @ Dr.
Rajan Gupta, applicant no.2- Rajrani and applicant no.3-Gaurav Gupta seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.0182 of 2021, under Sections 498-A, 323, 506, 376, 326, 511 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Madnapur, District- Shahjahanpur.

It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicants that applicants are innocent and they have apprehension of their arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against them.
Allegations levelled against the applicants are false.
The investigation of the case has been completed and charge-sheet has been filed and cognizance has been taken by the Court concerned.
Process under Sections 82 and 83 CrPC have also been issued against the applicants.
It has been submitted that in case applicants are granted anticipatory bail, they shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that accused has no role in the present matter and it is trend now-a-days to rope the whole family of the husband of the aggrieved wife in such type of cases.
It is further submitted that charge sheet in the matter has been filed and the accused applicants have provided their cooperation during the investigation.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the original informant vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that the offence levelled against the present applicants is very serious.
Accused applicant no.1 has committed sexual offence with the victim of the case who happens to be his daughter-in-law.
After collecting sufficient evidence during the course of investigation, now the charge sheet has been submitted against him.
In her statement u/s 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix has fully corroborated the F.I.R. version and as such anticipatory bail application is liable to be rejected.

In the present case, apart from this allegation regarding cruelty and harassment caused by in-laws of the victim, a specific allegation has been made against the accused applicant no.1 in respect of sexual offence with the victim of the case.
The accused-applicant no.1 is said to be the father-in-law of the victim.
After collecting sufficient evidence during the course of investigation, now the charge sheet has been filed against the applicants.

In the facts and circumstances of the present case, this is not a case of simple harassment caused to the victim lady on account of the aforesaid demand but it is a case where specific allegations against the accused applicant no.1-the father-in-law have been levelled by the victim lady.

The attention of this Court is drawn to the fact that Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No.27850 of 2022 was filed by the present accused-applicants wherein order for mediation was passed on 12.09.2022 and it was directed that for a period of six months from that day or till completion of mediation proceedings, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case.
It was brought to the notice of this Court that mediation proceedings are failed and the said application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. has been finally disposed of vide order dated 12.09.2022.
In this matter, it reveals that after completion of investigation, charge sheet has been submitted and cognizance has also been taken by the Court concerned.
Summons were issued to the applicant.
Since the applicant did not appear before the Court concerned, coercive processes have been issued against them.

In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1,
the Hon'ble Apex Court has settled the controversy finally by holding the anticipatory bail need not be of limited duration invariably.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In appropriate case, it can continue upto conclusion of trial.
It has been further held therein that anticipatory bail granted can, depending on the conduct and behavior of the accused, continue after filing of the charge sheet till end of trial.

It has been further held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, llikelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity Dr Rajendra Kumar Gupta @ Dr Rajan Gupta ... vs State Of U.P.And Another on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154072292/
2 of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.
It appears from a perusal of the record that in this matter after investigation charge sheet has been submitted against the applicants.
Summon was issued against them.
Since the applicants did not appear before the Court concerned, punitive actions were taken against them, as they were absconding.
Process under Sections 82 and 83 CrPC were issued against them.
The conduct of the applicants fall within the ambit of the law promulgated by Hon'ble Apex Court in Prem Shankar Prasad Versus State of Bihar and Another, 2021 SCC OnLine Supreme Court 955.

entities.text: Prem Shankar Prasad Versus State of Bihar and Another, 2021 SCC OnLine Supreme Court 955
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the facts of the case, charge-sheet was filed under Sections 406, 420 IPC against the accused and thus it was explicit that a prima facie case against the accused was found.

From the record, it reveals that the arrest warrant was issued by the Magistrate against the accused and thereafter proceedings under Sections 82, 83 Cr.P.C. had been initiated pursuant to the order passed by the Magistrate.
Only thereafter the accused moved an application before the trial court for anticipatory bail, which was rejected by the Sessions Court.
However, subsequently anticipatory bail was granted to the aforesaid accused by the High Court and when the matter came before the Hon'ble Apex Court, it was observed like this.

"19. Despite the above observations on merits and despite the fact that it was brought to the notice of the High Court that respondent No. 2 - accused is absconding and even the proceedings under sections 82-83 of Cr. P.C. have been initiated as far as back on 10.01.2019, the High Court has just ignored the aforesaid relevant aspects and has granted anticipatory bail to respondent No. 2 - accused by observing that the nature of accusation is arising out of a business transaction.
The specific allegations of cheating, etc., which came to be considered by learned Additional Sessions Judge has not at all been considered by the High Court.
Even the High Court has just ignored the factum of initiation of proceedings under sections 82-83 of Cr. P.C. by simply observing that "be that as it may".
The aforesaid relevant aspect on grant of anticipatory bail ought not to have been ignored by the High Court and ought to have been considered by the High Court very seriously and not casually.

20. In the case of State of Madhya Pradesh v. Pradeep Sharma (Supra), it is observed and held by this court that if anyone is declared as an absconder/proclaimed offender in terms of section 82 of Cr. P.C., he is not entitled to relief of anticipatory bail."

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Pradeep Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, I deem it not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the present applicant.
Such a person, who does not cooperate in the matter, is not entitled for any relief from this Court by way of granting anticipatory bail.
Prayer made in the application is refused.
The anticipatory bail application is rejected.
